change: Add isolated Vite and Playwright configurations for the existing React application against qualified private browser/Wasm packages. Reuse the browser candidate's package-record, archive and installed-tree checks. Build only under target/react-demo-candidate and use a candidate-local Vite cache. Preserve default application config, shipping dist trees, test assertions, per-case/global deadlines, one worker and zero retries. No editor runtime change.

tests.scope: Eleven application cases and two autosave-observation helper cases per engine, using Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Application checks cover conflicting-tab backup without overwriting the winning save, fault-time Rust backup, invalid UTF-8 rejection, editing/format/history/autosave/recovery, shortcuts, size/color/Link controls, accessibility and trailing-space typing. This is compatibility of the existing paragraph-profile React app, not an end-to-end heading/list UI test; the separate list demo supplies that evidence.

additionalChecks: Strict demo/test/config TypeScript passed after correcting three TS4111 index-signature property accesses in the new config. The initial typecheck failed before any browser test started.
Vite configuration loading with no candidate record and with package.json as an out-of-target record rejected before a build. Expected rejection assertions passed.
A second isolated production build produced a byte-identical complete output tree.
All four shipping artifact tree hashes match the candidate package qualification baseline after both builds.
budgetNote: Comparisons use unchanged limits from scripts/check-size-budgets.mjs, applied to the isolated candidate assets rather than shipping paths. Gzip-9 is measured explicitly, not Vite's default gzip display. No budget was raised; these results do not pass the production-size gate.
limits: The target output directory is shared by this qualification config; schedule runs sequentially. This config is not a delivery/package naming decision or a complete release verifier. Native physical input/IME/VoiceOver, current-artifact native qualification, larger-list responsiveness and delivery/size approval remain open. Historical WebKit issues are not cleared by a finite passing suite.
